items.stem: In GitOps with Argo CD, where is the desired state of the system defined?

options.text: In a Git repository, which Argo CD continuously reconciles against the cluster
options.rationale: Correct: Git is the single source of truth and Argo CD pulls and reconciles it.

options.text: Only in the live cluster, edited directly with kubectl
options.rationale: Direct cluster edits are drift; Git is the source of truth in GitOps.

options.text: In Argo CD's memory only, never persisted
options.rationale: Desired state is persisted in Git, not just in memory.

options.text: In a spreadsheet maintained by the operations team
options.rationale: A spreadsheet is not a reconciled source of truth.

items.explanation: Correct: Git is the single source of truth and Argo CD pulls and reconciles it.

items.stem: Which two behaviours does Argo CD's self-healing / reconciliation provide? (Select TWO)

options.text: It detects when the cluster drifts from the desired state in Git
It can automatically revert manual changes back to the Git-defined state
options.rationale: Correct: with self-heal enabled, drift is corrected back to desired state.

options.text: It deletes the Git repository after each sync
options.rationale: Argo CD relies on the repo; it does not delete it.

options.text: It randomly changes the desired state on its own
options.rationale: Argo CD applies the declared state, it does not invent changes.

items.explanation: Correct: continuous comparison detects drift.; Correct: with self-heal enabled, drift is corrected back to desired state.

items.stem: What is the purpose of the app-of-apps pattern in Argo CD?

options.text: A parent Application manages a set of child Applications declaratively
options.rationale: Correct: app-of-apps lets one Application bootstrap and manage many others from Git.

options.text: It merges all microservices into a single container
options.rationale: It manages Applications, not container packaging.

options.text: It disables GitOps for child applications
options.rationale: Children are still managed via GitOps.

options.text: It stores secrets in plaintext by default
options.rationale: The pattern is about structure, not secret handling.

items.explanation: Correct: app-of-apps lets one Application bootstrap and manage many others from Git.
